name: Banh uot thit nuong
summary: Hot grilled meat rolled in soft wet rice paper with herbs, cucumber, star fruit, and green banana, then dipped. Some stalls grill pork on lemongrass skewers for a dip of soybean paste, peanuts, sesame, and chili; others roll grilled beef with a rich, mildly hot peanut sauce.
origin: Hoi An. Vietnam Tourism lists it with the town’s food. The conservation centre’s 4 September 2024 article, republishing Dân Việt, places stalls along the Hoài river.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism stacks grilled pork from lemongrass skewers with salad, herbs, cucumber, and star fruit, wraps them in wet rice paper, and dips them in soybean paste, peanuts, sesame, fish sauce, and chili.
The 4 December 2025 article rolls grilled beef and dips it in a rich, mildly hot peanut-butter sauce.

Danang Fantasticity’s 16 April 2024 essay says hot grilled meat, Trà Quế herbs, green banana, cucumber, and a sauce it calls special. It names a sweet sauce, fragrant meat, chili, and astringent herbs.
The 4 September 2024 article says grilled skewers with a little peanut, herbs, and a salty-sweet dip, along the Hoài. Keep every account.
where: Stalls along the Hoài river, on the 4 September 2024 article.
seoTitle: Banh uot thit nuong — Hoi An grilled rolls
seoDescription: Bánh ướt thịt nướng in Hoi An is a roll you build. Vietnam Tourism says pork. A December 2025 article says beef.
